plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 after compilation failure due to material identifier truncation ('si' instead of 'sio2'). Three routes proposed: (1) Ge/ZnS 2-cavity Fabry-Perot with 20 layers fixing material naming, (2) Ge/YbF3 18-layer alternative material pair for stress management, (3) Si/ZnSe 22-layer design exploring different high-index material. All routes use explicit layer counts, valid material identifiers, and optimizable thickness variables. Parent route ID preserved as route_01 per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot Dual-Bandpass Filter with 20 Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) quarter-wave stacks on CaF2 substrate can achieve simultaneous transmission peaks at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm with strong blocking in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands within 20 layers.
routes.design_principle: Start with alternating quarter-wave layers at center wavelengths of each passband, form two coupled Fabry-Perot cavities separated by Bragg reflectors, then computationally optimize all layer thicknesses to shape dual passbands while maintaining stopband rejection. Ge/ZnS pair provides high index contrast (~4.0/2.3) for mid-IR with low absorption.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge cavity1 | [ZnS/Ge]_3 | ZnS cavity2 | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Air incident. Total finite layers: 20 (10 Ge + 10 ZnS).
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are standard mid-IR coating materials
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for layered media
expected_advantages: High index contrast enables fewer layers for given blocking
Ge/ZnS pair verified for 3-5 μm mid-IR range
Two-cavity design allows dual passband shaping
known_risks: Ge absorption may increase beyond 5 μm
Stress mismatch between Ge and ZnS
Fabrication tolerance sensitivity for narrow bands
routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 20-layer dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-bandpass transmission. Layer stack: CaF2 | Layer1(Ge) | Layer2(ZnS) | Layer3(Ge) | Layer4(ZnS) | Layer5(Ge) | Layer6(ZnS) | Layer7(Ge) | Layer8(ZnS) | Layer9(Ge) | Layer10(ZnS) | Layer11(Ge) | Layer12(ZnS) | Layer13(Ge) | Layer14(ZnS) | Layer15(Ge) | Layer16(ZnS) | Layer17(Ge) | Layer18(ZnS) | Layer19(Ge) | Layer20(ZnS) | Air. Optimize all 20 layer thicknesses in range 100-2000 nm. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm with dense sampling. Incident medium: Air at 0 degrees. Substrate: CaF2. Target: maximize transmittance in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm bands, minimize transmittance in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm bands. Use multi-objective optimization with weighted spectral averaging. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Previous route failed compilation due to material identifier truncation ('si' instead of 'sio2'). This route uses explicit valid material names (Ge, ZnS, CaF2) and fixes the layer specification to be TMM-compiler compatible. Topology changed from periodic stack to 2-cavity Fabry-Perot based on evidence for dual-bandpass applications.

routes.title: Ge/YbF3 Three-Cavity Design with 18 Layers for Reduced Stress
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A three-cavity Fabry-Perot filter using Ge (high-index) and YbF3 (low-index) can achieve dual-bandpass transmission with better stress matching than Ge/ZnS, enabling more stable fabrication within 18 layers.
routes.design_principle: Three coupled cavities provide more degrees of freedom for shaping dual passbands. YbF3 has lower stress than ZnS when deposited with Ge. Quarter-wave Bragg mirrors surround each cavity spacer, with cavity thicknesses tuned to create transmission peaks at target wavelengths.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Ge/YbF3]_3 | Ge cavity1 | [YbF3/Ge]_2 | YbF3 cavity2 | [Ge/YbF3]_2 | Ge cavity3 | [YbF3/Ge]_3 | Air incident. Total finite layers: 18 (9 Ge + 9 YbF3).
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: YbF3 has lower stress than ZnS for mid-IR coatings
Ge/YbF3 pair compatible with conventional deposition
expected_advantages: Three cavities provide more spectral shaping freedom
18 layers leaves margin for manufacturing tolerance
known_risks: YbF3 refractive index lower than ZnS may require more layers
Ge absorption characteristics must be verified

Layer stack: CaF2 | Layer1(Ge) | Layer2(YbF3) | Layer3(Ge) | Layer4(YbF3) | Layer5(Ge) | Layer6(YbF3) | Layer7(Ge) | Layer8(YbF3) | Layer9(Ge) | Layer10(YbF3) | Layer11(Ge) | Layer12(YbF3) | Layer13(Ge) | Layer14(YbF3) | Layer15(Ge) | Layer16(YbF3) | Layer17(Ge) | Layer18(YbF3) | Air. Optimize all 18 layer thicknesses in range 150-2500 nm. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm with dense sampling. Incident medium: Air at 0 degrees. Substrate: CaF2. Target: maximize transmittance in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm bands, minimize transmittance in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm bands. Use global optimization with cavity-resonance initialization. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Alternative material pair (Ge/YbF3 vs Ge/ZnS) to address potential stress issues from route_01_refine_01. Different cavity count (3 vs 2) provides complementary design space exploration. Layer count reduced to 18 to test if fewer layers can achieve similar performance.

routes.title: Si/ZnSe High-Contrast Stack with 22 Layers for Maximum Blocking
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A Si (high-index ~3.4) and ZnSe (low-index ~2.4) periodic stack with 22 layers can achieve stronger stopband blocking than Ge-based designs due to better material transparency beyond 5 μm, while maintaining dual passbands through thickness optimization.
routes.design_principle: Si/ZnSe pair provides good index contrast with lower absorption in 4.85-5.20 μm stopband compared to Ge. Use periodic Bragg stack as base, then introduce thickness perturbations to create dual transmission peaks. Higher layer count (22) compensates for lower index contrast.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Si/ZnSe]_11 | Air incident. Total finite layers: 22 (11 Si + 11 ZnSe). Periodic quarter-wave stack with optimized thickness deviations.
design_variables: quarter-wave deviation factors for each layer
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: Si and ZnSe are conventional IR deposition materials
Higher layer count increases deposition time
theory_basis: Index contrast vs layer count trade-off
expected_advantages: Si/ZnSe has lower absorption in 5+ μm range than Ge
known_risks: Lower index contrast than Ge/ZnS may require more layers for same blocking
Si absorption in near-IR may affect short wavelength edge

Layer stack: CaF2 | Layer1(Si) | Layer2(ZnSe) | Layer3(Si) | Layer4(ZnSe) | Layer5(Si) | Layer6(ZnSe) | Layer7(Si) | Layer8(ZnSe) | Layer9(Si) | Layer10(ZnSe) | Layer11(Si) | Layer12(ZnSe) | Layer13(Si) | Layer14(ZnSe) | Layer15(Si) | Layer16(ZnSe) | Layer17(Si) | Layer18(ZnSe) | Layer19(Si) | Layer20(ZnSe) | Layer21(Si) | Layer22(ZnSe) | Air. Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses in range 200-1800 nm. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm with dense sampling. Incident medium: Air at 0 degrees. Substrate: CaF2. Target: maximize transmittance in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm bands, minimize transmittance in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm bands. Initialize from quarter-wave stack at 4400 nm center, then optimize with gradient-based method. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Third complementary route exploring different material system (Si/ZnSe vs Ge-based) to address potential Ge absorption issues in 4.85-5.20 μm stopband. Higher layer count (22) tests whether increased design freedom compensates for lower index contrast. Provides fallback if Ge-based routes fail.
